W.note: Syllables run 5-8-6 ("the cloud's edge turns mother-of-pearl" is 8, "then the blue takes it back" is 6), so the form is loose, though the sun-below-ridge to pearl-edge to blue turn evokes iridescence well.

X.note: Exact 5-7-5 (Na-cre-ous light blooms / high above the frozen fjord / a cloud gone by dawn), and nacreous clouds over a polar fjord are an accurate real phenomenon, with the dawn fade giving a clean ending.

Y.note: Exact 5-7-5 (lens cloud on the ridge / the wind pours through it all day / the cloud does not move), and the stationary lenticular cloud with wind passing through it is a true, well-chosen paradox that lands as the turn.

Z.note: Exact 5-7-5 (sil-ver threads at dusk / clouds no com-mon sky can make / hang where no one looks), and the silver dusk threads accurately evoke noctilucent clouds, though "no common sky" stays vague and "silver threads" is a near-stock image.
